_about: The N360 customer risk model (docs/21_RISK_MODEL.md). Every feature, weight, anchor, hard red and model setting is here; code never holds a threshold. All values are PROPOSED until Ryan approves and the backtest supports them.
_label_about: The unit is the renewal of an ACCOUNT (its largest contract line's end date; code/risk/features.py). A snapshot belongs to the customer's next renewal when it is 0 to eligible_days_to_renewal days away (unknown renewal date: not judged); dates within same_renewal_days of each other are one renewal. The renewal's outcome is the churn, downsell or renewal recorded from the day the customer entered the renewal window (so an early opt-out is not missed; never later than outcome_days_before) to outcome_days_after past the date. A renewal with nothing recorded counts as kept ONLY when a contract was still running after the date; otherwise it is unconfirmed and not used. Snapshots taken once the outcome was recorded, and every snapshot after a churn, are never used. A churned customer stays in the scores for churned_keep_days with the band 'churned'.
_features_about: risk = clamp((value - good) / (bad - good), 0, 1): 0 at or better than good, 1 at or worse than bad (works in either direction). weight = share inside its dimension. pit = can be computed as it stood on a past date (point-in-time); features that cannot are left out of training and backtests and used only for today's score. Two features that measure nearly the same thing share weight rather than double it: pace gap is the smaller partner of forecast at term end, and the 12-week volume change of the 4-week one.

bands._about: Under min_coverage (share of the model's weight with data) and with no hard red, the band is 'not enough data': too little is known to call the customer healthy.

probability._about: Chance of churn or downsell at the next renewal. It starts as an expert prior: a customer at the average scorecard risk (prior_mean_risk) gets prior_mean_rate (set this from the real renewal record: renewals lost / renewals due), a customer at full risk everywhere gets prior_max_rate, and features move the log-odds in proportion to their scorecard weights. The prior's level is fixed: the same readings give the same chance on any day. Until a run is adopted it is the level these settings give; 'train' sets it once on every stored snapshot of customers in their renewal window (at least prior_level_min_snapshots of them), so that their average chance is prior_mean_rate, and the level stays with that run. It then learns in stages, counted in DISTINCT renewals lost (and as many kept): from stages.calibrate the level and one slope (the prior's level counts as prior_strength_renewals renewals of evidence, so the first few outcomes move it gently); from stages.dimension one weight per dimension; from stages.feature one weight per feature. ridge_lambda is relative: a weight's prior spread is its prior value / sqrt(ridge_lambda), so 4 means the data must argue to move a weight by half. Weights never go below zero.

backtest._about: Walk-forward: retrain every train_every_days once min_train_days of history exist; training uses one snapshot per renewal every train_sample_days, weighted so each renewal counts once. Each renewal is judged at lead_days before it (the nearest snapshot within lead_tolerance_days). top_share = the share flagged when measuring precision. Intervals: `bootstrap` resamples of whole customers. alert_probability = the chance at which the model counts as having warned; hold_days = how long before a loss the warning must still be up. without_dimensions: the scorecard is also judged with these dimensions blanked (the CSM's own rating and register often follow the customer saying it is leaving, so they can flatter a backtest).
